title: Wizard's Office Liaisons: What's on your desk this week?
notice: Synthetic demo material. Invented document; no real meeting, publication, email or call occurred.

blocks.text: Posted by Rowan Bell: Liaisons, you're our bridge between the network and the city. What's a small, real piece of work on your desk right now—something approved, translated, drafted, or collected? Keen to hear what that looks like.

Ivy Coppermore here. Just processed a permit for a temporary safety fence around a sidewalk repair on Spectacle Lane. The contractor's paperwork was all in order—liability insurance current, dimensions to spec. It's a three-foot wooden barrier, goes up Monday. It feels minor, but it's the sort of thing that keeps a pedestrian from twisting an ankle in a hole. The approval took ten minutes once the file was complete.

Delphine Saffronmere. Less about permits, more about geography! The little schoolhouse at Brickway Junction is consolidating its library, and they were clearing out old teaching aids. I collected a set of slightly outdated but perfectly serviceable globes and wall maps. They've got that lovely, worn-in patina. They're for my tutoring space—makes a world of difference for the students to see the shape of things, even if some of the borders are a few decades old. Practical and atmospheric.

Teo Orchardwood! My desk is covered in meal descriptions and activity logs—in Quadling, Gillikin, and a dash of old Winkie dialect. Just finished translating a full month's worth of daily menus and schedules for Lantern Row Care Home. The goal is inclusion, right? Now residents who are more comfortable in their first languages can know if it's stew day or music hour without having to ask. It's meticulous work (the word for 'meatloaf' is surprisingly contentious across regions), but so worth it.

Willa Rushwick. Currently drafting a funding proposal for the Wizard's Office. The new terrace gardens on the west embankment are thriving, but they're all hauling watering cans from a single tap two blocks away. The proposal is for a shared, centrally-located water line with multiple outlets. It's in the early stages—mapping current use, projecting water savings, outlining the shared maintenance agreement between the gardeners. Hoping to submit it for the next quarter's civic improvements budget.
Willa, that's a good one. Let me know if you need any precedent permits for subsurface utility work when you get to that stage. There's a standard form for shared infrastructure on city land.

Teo, that's wonderful. It's those daily details that make a place feel like home. And Willa, good luck with the proposal. Our Brickway Junction community garden would have folded years ago without a proper water source.
Appreciate the fence permit, Ivy. Walk past that spot every day with my kids. Nice to know it's being handled properly.

Delphine, your maps sound fantastic! And thank you, Ivy—precise paperwork is its own kind of poetry. Willa, I'd be happy to look over any public-facing summaries of your proposal for clarity, if useful. Jargon is a beast in any language.
